evaluationParameters: Continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide trend and adequacy of ventilation
missingInformation: Identity and dose of the volatile anesthetic and whether succinylcholine was administered
Arterial blood gas, serum potassium, creatine kinase, acid-base status, and urine findings for complications and severity
priorityActions: Immediately discontinue the volatile anesthetic and ventilate with 100% oxygen using a clean anesthesia circuit or activated charcoal filters.
Administer intravenous dantrolene promptly according to the malignant hyperthermia protocol.
reasoning: The combination of unexplained rapidly increasing carbon dioxide production, tachycardia, generalized rigidity, and rapidly rising core temperature after exposure to a volatile anesthetic is the classic perioperative presentation of malignant hyperthermia. Immediate trigger removal, maximal oxygenation and ventilation, and dantrolene are time-critical; falling end-tidal carbon dioxide and core temperature help demonstrate treatment response.
stemEvidence: Rapid, marked rise in end-tidal carbon dioxide despite increased minute ventilation
Rapid increase in core temperature during volatile-anesthetic exposure
